instruction: Open /home/user/Desktop/drill_plate.step in FreeCAD 0.21.2 Path/CAM. Open the part in FreeCAD from `/usr/bin/freecad`, then carry out the Path workbench edits when working on `drill_plate.step`. The STEP is one 120 x 80 x 12 mm plate in source coordinates X=-60..60, Y=-40..40, Z=0..12, with four D2 x 0.25 mm shallow circular location marks on the top face at (X,Y)=(-25,-15), (-25,15), (25,-15), and (25,15). Create one native Path Job, use the model bounding box as stock with zero extension, and set G54 at the plate XY center and top face so the Job model is Z=-12..0. Create exactly two active native Drilling operations in this order and use only those four marked centers in each operation. First, use ToolController T1 with a native drill ToolBit whose full TipAngle is 90 degrees as the spot drill; choose a practical positive tool diameter, set clockwise S8000 rpm with horizontal and vertical feed 250 mm/min, and make a shallow spot that continues below the existing Z=-0.25 mm mark floor so it removes material, without going deeper than 3 mm or past the 90-degree conical tip. Second, use ToolController T2 with a native D5 mm drill ToolBit; set clockwise S5000 rpm with horizontal and vertical feed 180 mm/min, set the nominal FinalDepth to Z=-13 mm, and use the native Drill Tip ExtraOffset so the full D5 diameter clears the Z=-12 bottom face by 1 mm. Use safe positive retract, safe, and clearance heights between holes; G98 or a safe G99 retract is acceptable. Recompute and verify both native toolpaths, keep the editable document clean and up-to-date, post in metric absolute G54 with the native linuxcnc postprocessor, save the editable document exactly as /home/user/Desktop/task-3.FCStd, and write the matching NC exactly as /home/user/Desktop/task-3.nc.
